geometry: 2D decaying Taylor-Green vortex, doubly periodic, N x N domain, kx=ky=2*PI/N (one wavelength fills the domain exactly)
note: EXACT closed-form space-time solution (velocity field at every point AND time, not just steady state) -- see main-tgv.js's own header for the derivation. field_l2_tol bounds the worst-case (over checkpoints) relative L2 error of the simulated velocity field against the analytic field; decay_rate_tol bounds the relative error between the fitted RMS-velocity decay rate (measured between the last two checkpoints) and the analytic 1/td. checkpoints are given as multiples of the analytic decay time td so the same sample points (chosen to skip the brief initial-condition transient any equilibrium-distribution IC seed produces -- see main-tgv.js's own initF comment) are used regardless of N/u0/tau. AMR cases (levels present) run against index-tgv-amr.html at the SAME N as a same-named dense case would use, with autoRefine left at its default (on, but with conservative thresholds that don't trigger for these u0/N choices -- see main-tgv-amr.js's own header on the large-scale-simultaneous-refinement fragility this deliberately avoids triggering) -- the check here is 'does the AMR machinery reproduce the dense-equivalent decay when idle,' not a refinement-pattern accuracy study.

measurement.checkpoints_meaning: multiples of td=1/(nu*(kx^2+ky^2)), converted to a step count and rounded per case at run time
measurement.decay_rate: fit via -ln(rms(t_b)/rms(t_a))/(t_b-t_a) between the last two checkpoints, rms = sqrt(mean(ux^2+uy^2)) over the field
